dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The West-dealer annual rows have unique `source_event_id` values, and the import log reports no duplicate source events."
"The two May dealer files accepted every received row and reconciled cash to ledger with zero difference and zero duplicate-source-event flags."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 90 West-dealer annual rows have effective dates in the same calendar month as their posting dates; the May rows have effective dates from 1–28 May and post on 31 May."
"Cross-referencing `email-dealer-reconciliation.eml` with `recharges.csv` indicates that transaction clustering is an operational batching artifact rather than commercial manipulation."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Unknowns and Decision-Changing Evidence"
"This inference firmly resolves data-pipeline and fraud hypotheses, while leaving revenue-recognition policy and entitlement activation as the two explicit open unknowns."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The single next action is one read-only verification query comparing the West-dealer trend by `posted_at` and `effective_event_date`, alongside a small entitlement sample."
"If policy requires effective-date reporting or the sample finds failed activation, escalate that specific issue; otherwise close the anomaly as reconciled posting timing."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: No material irregularity detected; do not escalate or alter existing postings."
"Keep restatement on hold pending the result."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "All source events are unique and cash reconciles to the ledger with zero variance, showing no evidence of fake revenue." The checks strongly reduce duplicate-revenue risk but do not by themselves prove that revenue was not fabricated or that the reconciliation controls are complete and reliable.

"Observed facts confirm complete row acceptance, unique source identifiers, and exact dollar reconciliation across all dealer import files in `dealer_import_log.csv`." The cited detail specifically names DF-00020 and DF-00040; the broader claim about all dealer import files is not fully demonstrated in the submission.

"This inference firmly resolves data-pipeline and fraud hypotheses." The evidence makes those explanations less likely, but does not fully resolve fraud or every possible pipeline defect without validating control completeness and downstream effects.
"do not escalate" is somewhat premature because entitlement activation has not yet been tested; the submission appropriately makes escalation conditional later.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled duplicate revenue, manipulation, backdating, and reporting-policy alternatives well, but the strongest unresolved alternative is a provisioning or entitlement defect: financial reconciliation can be clean while some subscribers fail to receive valid activation. That risk is identified but not yet tested.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform and report the entitlement check for a risk-based sample of the 90 West-dealer annual accounts, while explicitly comparing posted-time and effective-event-time outputs; this would align the conclusion with the stated condition that escalation is unnecessary only if both financial and entitlement checks reconcile.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Under legacy routing, South had 219 `case_create` sessions out of 442 legacy South sessions; under NOVA-S1, only 90 of 2,709 sessions reached `case_create`."
"South NO_SIGNAL tickets fell from 51 in May to 28 in June, but service-event data still records 10 May events affecting 9,409 accounts and 8 June events affecting 7,045 accounts."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "complaint volume was suppressed by channel filtering: 24.0% of sessions (650/2,709) in `ivr_interactions.jsonl` dropped out at the authentication stage without creating CareDesk tickets."
"The pilot email says sessions ending before authentication are monitored in the technical pilot report rather than CareDesk because no verified customer context exists."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "I cannot determine whether dropped authentication sessions resulted in callbacks without a read-only 7-day recontact trace."
"existing recovery queues justify continuing the pilot; unaddressed drop-offs require fixing authentication before any expansion."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Defer national expansion and maintain existing South pilot boundaries."
"The single next action is a read-only subscriber callback reconciliation query... zero database writes, zero routing changes."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Person: Farah Iqbal, Customer Care Operations, because she owns IVR journey stages, case-creation conditions, and the containment definition."
"What written pass threshold and observation window govern pilot-to-national expansion?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Apparent complaint reduction is heavily driven by 650 pre-authentication drops and automated ticket-creation suppression rather than verified self-service resolution." The evidence supports missing case creation and exclusion from the CareDesk view, but does not establish that the drops were complaints, that suppression was automated, or that this was the main driver of the overall reduction.

"Underlying network faults persisted at 8 to 10 major service events per month." Only May and June are cited, and the submission does not establish that all listed events were major network faults or that this is a stable monthly pattern.
"pre-authentication drop-offs in `ivr_interactions.jsonl` tripled to 24.0%" No earlier percentage or directly comparable baseline is provided to substantiate 'tripled.'
"unresolved technical issues went unrecorded." The data show sessions without verified case creation, not that those sessions involved unresolved technical issues.

"This divergence refutes the claim that fewer logged tickets prove fewer customer issues." It appropriately challenges the claim, but service-event counts and ticket counts are not expected to move one-for-one, so 'refutes' is stronger than the evidence warrants.

"It is completely reversible and low cost." Read-only and no-write properties support reversibility, but cost and privacy/operational implications of subscriber-level reconciliation are not demonstrated.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles the main benign alternative that authentication failures may have been recovered downstream or that genuine containment occurred, stating that low repeat-contact rates could support genuine containment and that routine queries may have been deflected. It does not fully test this alternative with linked journey outcomes or sampled call listening, and it treats authentication-stage abandonment too readily as evidence of complaint suppression.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add end-to-end validation beyond repeat contacts: link authentication failures to subsequent outcomes and manually sample calls, while explicitly checking the South-only break around the 10 May rollout and avoiding unsupported claims that abandonment represents complaints.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, and specific fields for `event`, `severity`, `duration_min`, `impact_mw`, `cleared`, `timestamp_local`, and `inverter_id`.
The claims that all four rows have zero impact and are cleared, and that the 7-minute warning is the strongest event, are directly traceable to cited fields.
The phrase “zero repeat pattern” is supported only within this export and should have been explicitly scoped to the file.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The analyst distinguishes event labels from demonstrated equipment failure: “Labels alone do not establish failure.”
The analyst tests the plausible scope/completeness explanation and proposes an unfiltered read-only query rather than inventing a plant mechanism.
The reasoning relies on one event export rather than independent telemetry or communications channels, although the available evidence supports justified stopping.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly notes that the export has only four rows and lacks a plant-wide denominator or extraction-filter information.
It conditions the decision on the unfiltered pull revealing “recurrence, open status, critical severity, or nonzero generation impact.”
It appropriately distinguishes a data-scope check from evidence of an equipment fault and does not claim to prove the export is complete.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation and make no equipment change” is proportionate to four short, cleared, zero-impact records.
The proposed same-date, unfiltered, read-only export is reversible and discriminates between a complete benign extract and a filtered extract concealing materially different events.
The action preserves operational safety without escalating based solely on a seven-minute communications warning.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly identifies the visible records as low-signal: all are cleared, have `impact_mw=0`, involve four distinct inverters, and total 13 minutes.
It accurately limits the conclusion to the supplied file and makes completeness the only worthwhile follow-up.
The recommendation is consistent with the evidence and with justified stopping rather than searching for an unsupported story.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Zero repeat pattern” is too broad unless qualified as no recurrence within this export; the file cannot establish behavior outside its scope.

“Escalation requires empirical telemetry showing persisted megawatt loss” is overgeneralized. An open, critical, recurring, or safety-relevant event could justify escalation even before persistent MW loss is demonstrated.
“Do not escalate any event from this file” is reasonable operationally but should remain conditional on confirming that the export is not filtered or incomplete.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export may be incomplete or filtered, so the four benign-looking records could underrepresent open, critical, recurring, or nonzero-impact events elsewhere in the same date range. The analyst appropriately treats this as a completeness hypothesis rather than evidence of a plant fault.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run and retain the unfiltered same-date export, including extraction metadata or filter settings; this directly tests whether the apparent absence of recurrence, open status, critical severity, and impact is real.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific files and fields, including `dispatch_blocks.csv`, `base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`, and `schedule_source`.
It explicitly separates observation from inference: “High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation.”
It reproduces both the cross-day calculation, `(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%`, and the same-day modeled comparison of Rs 549,664 versus Rs 453,086.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission recognizes that the headline compares different dates and tests a same-day counterfactual using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May.
It triangulates penalty totals, schedule-source counts, firmware and wind fields, daily variability, and two definitions of deviation rather than relying on a single headline metric.

It considers innocent explanations and causal limitations, including selection/timing, lack of randomization, one-day replication, and the distinction between penalty reduction and net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission distinguishes “High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation” and states that the 17.6% figure “does not establish general causal efficacy.”

It identifies specific unknowns—whether comparator selection was outcome-informed, whether revisions preceded actual generation, repeatability, and net value—and specifies evidence that would change the decision.
It avoids both overclaiming the 31.6% result and overcorrecting to zero value.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to “place expansion on hold” follows from the absence of a controlled causal estimate while preserving the observed same-day association.
The proposed prospective shadow validation uses pre-registered matched high-wind stow days, immutable timestamps, and reconciled net settlement, making it a discriminating and low-risk next test.

The action preserves operational constraints because it is explicitly “read-only,” does not change submitted schedules or plant control, and includes energy revenue, DSM penalty, and pilot cost considerations.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately states: “Credit the arithmetic, reject the attribution—the defensible within-day figure is ~17.6%, not 31.6%.”
It keeps the smaller same-day benefit rather than claiming no value, while limiting 31.6% to a descriptive cross-day difference and 17.6% to a modeled one-day estimate.
This directly addresses the central causal limitation that 28 May is a different, unusually high-penalty day and is not established as a valid control.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the proposed shadow calculation is “fully reversible” is reasonable as an operational characterization but is not directly evidenced by the cited source files.

The claim that the two dates have “similar listed wind fields” is observed as presented, but similarity in listed wind fields alone does not establish comparability; the submission appropriately does not use it to claim causality.

The same-day 17.6% estimate remains model-dependent because it treats `base_schedule_mw` as the counterfactual and uses realized generation; the submission clearly labels this limitation rather than presenting it as an established causal effect.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have produced a genuine but smaller reduction in modeled DSM penalty on 29 May, while the 31.6% cross-day difference may partly or substantially reflect day selection, weather, operational conditions, or regression from the unusually high 28 May penalty. The available evidence cannot identify the causal share or establish net commercial value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add and analyze immutable pre-submission forecast and schedule timestamps, together with a pre-registered matched-day comparator rule and complete net-settlement data, so the same-day counterfactual and any timing or selection effects can be tested prospectively.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declaration: P1001 declared with 90211000." Source: `declaration.pdf`, line 1
"Swiss row: P1001=90211000 from 2025-01-01." Source: `country_tariff_matrix.xlsx`, P1001
"commercial_invoice.pdf confirms P1001, 10 units, CHF 126,900 and `air_waybill.pdf` links SHP-000522 to CH-2025-000522."
"The open question is Swiss legal code on 4 November 2025."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Any differing string proves an error’: rejected because the Swiss reference lists 90211000 and warns Swiss/EU strings need not match."
"‘Helios is customs truth’: rejected because its Read Me calls it commercial data, not ruling status."
"A contradictory code flips decision to escalate; 90211000 closes review."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Swiss Matrix supports declared code but requires Tares confirmation."
"Neither proves legal classification."
"No record contradicts 90211000."
"Verification, not broker escalation, is proper."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "both share HS6 902110; local suffixes differ."
"`canonical-schema-v0.3.md` lacks jurisdiction and version metadata, so direct string comparison cannot prove error."
"Resolving schema deficiencies prevents repetitive false positives across Swiss entries."
"Helios ... is commercial data, not ruling authority."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares or ruling confirmation."
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive and add jurisdiction/version/date to the comparator."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Swiss Matrix confirms 90211000 is valid for Switzerland" is stronger than the submission's own qualification that the matrix requires Tares confirmation; the matrix appears to support the reference mapping, not independently establish legal validity.
"Mismatch is a control artifact rather than broker non-compliance" is a reasonable leading conclusion but remains provisional until the effective Swiss code on 2025-11-04 is confirmed.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is an absence-based claim and should be limited to the reviewed records and their coverage.
The claim that CHF 126,900 total would close the invoice-value issue is not fully explained; total-versus-unit value and any applicable customs-value rule remain unclear.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: 90211000 may have been invalid, superseded, or otherwise inapplicable on 2025-11-04 despite the matrix row beginning 2025-01-01, in which case the Helios difference could reflect a substantive classification or data-version issue rather than only a jurisdictional suffix mismatch. The submission appropriately identifies Tares or ruling confirmation as the decisive test.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the effective Swiss Tares or ruling record for P1001 on 2025-11-04, including its authority, version and effective date, before characterizing the mismatch as definitively benign.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`; the packet manifest lists six files and no shipment-specific supplier declaration."
"IE-2025-000411 declares P1006 with Preference=Yes, United States origin, 0.0% duty, and 90211090."
"The only Irish-origin register entry supplied for P1006 is SUP-02, valid 2025-01-01 to 2025-07-31 and marked ‘Expired in register’; the shipment date is 2025-09-18."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference indicator alone validates preferential treatment’: rejected because preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration"
"‘Commercial manufacturing country in commercial_invoice.pdf disproves preference’: rejected because manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preferential origin"

"‘The shipment should be flagged for fraud’: rejected because absence of a supplier declaration in `review_note.txt` and ClearView represents unverified documentation, not intentional misdeclaration."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Unsupported is not the same as false. Verdict: unsupported, not disproved."
"The register explicitly notes that absence from the table does not prove no document exists outside it."
"My inference is therefore limited to an evidence-control failure."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "none identifies the supplier route supporting preference."
"Automated check in `review_note.txt` flagged missing ClearView links."
"A supplier-linked declaration and applicable rule is the decision-changing proof."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible administrative hold on the preference claim."
"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral) until documentary proof is verified, without initiating an irreversible voluntary disclosure."
"The correct disposition is a reversible hold, not an error or fraud referral."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration" is stated categorically without establishing the applicable preference regime or showing that this is the only legally acceptable form of proof; the submission itself correctly identifies the applicable rule as still missing.

"valid EU supplier declarations exist for other suppliers in `supplier_origin_register.csv`" appears to treat register entries as declarations, although the cited source is described as a supplier origin register and the actual declarations are not identified.

"SUP-03/05/06 plus valid proof could support preference; SUP-01/US would support non-preferential treatment" is conditional and directionally useful, but supplier identity, sourcing route, and the applicable origin rule remain unresolved.

"Treat the line as non-preferential" may be operationally appropriate as an interim control, but the submission does not specify whether this is an internal hold, a customs filing position, or a duty reassessment; those consequences should be distinguished.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may be supportable: the shipment could have been sourced through SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06, or supporting documentation may exist outside the incomplete register. United States manufacturing country does not by itself determine preferential origin. The strongest present conclusion is therefore that the claim is unverified because supplier linkage, qualifying rule, and shipment-date coverage are missing—not that the claim is false or fraudulent.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State the applicable preference regime and test each permissible proof type against a reconstructed shipment-to-supplier data lineage, rather than treating an active linked supplier declaration as categorically required.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185 of 262 qcore_release_ts values are exactly 02:10:00"; "The SOP defines the routine target from required evidence being available"; "The 42 HOLD rows are open/right-censored".
Sources are tied to specific files, fields, counts, and quoted SOP sections, with some counterevidence and limitations acknowledged.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Headline cycle time of 1.5 days conflates physical receipt-to-release ... with the SOP-mandated evidence-to-release standard."
"Using lab_complete_ts as an approximation introduces uncontrolled error"
"true disposition time of 02:10 batches" is identified as a separate question to test.

The submission separates clock-definition problems, timestamp-interface effects, and right-censoring, while proposing audits that could discriminate among explanations. However, it labels the 02:10 values as defaulted/synthetic without direct proof and incorrectly refers to an evidence-to-release statistic when the evidence-availability timestamp is missing.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "missing/index-pending COA may be source lag rather than confirmed release without evidence"
"introduces uncontrolled error"
Confidence labels of "Medium-High" and "High" are provided.

Uncertainty is recognized, but the language "defaulted," "synthetic snapshot artifacts," and "evidence-to-release median" overstates what the extract establishes; the distinction between interface timestamp and decision timestamp should be kept explicit.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer KPI dashboard publication pending timestamp verification."
"The snapshot cannot compute compliance with SOP service targets"
"Next Verification Step: Execute a targeted read-only spot-check of 5–10 batches"
The recommendation appropriately reframes the task, avoids publishing a misleading KPI, is reversible and low-risk, and proposes a focused verification step rather than discarding usable data.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The 1.5-day headline reflects genuine process speed: rejected"
"Discard the extract as corrupt: rejected"
"Immediate dashboard release is safe: rejected"

Multiple alternatives are addressed with relevant evidence, including timestamp concentration, monotonic duration arithmetic, missing clock fields, and open HOLD rows. The strongest competing explanation—that timestamps are interface commits rather than decision times—is implied but not fully articulated or tested.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Live QCore timestamp audit capturing true certificate upload times"
"Read-only live audit of 10 batches with 02:10:00 extract timestamps"
"Execute a targeted read-only spot-check of 5–10 batches in live QCore and CertVault"

The requests are prioritized, small, operationally safe, and linked to explicit decision changes; they seek the minimum evidence needed to distinguish clock-definition and interface-timing hypotheses.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The claim that 185 timestamps are "defaulted" or "synthetic" is stronger than the observed fact that they are concentrated at 02:10:00 and coincide with a snapshot time; an interface commit or extraction behavior is not necessarily a defaulted value.

The phrase "excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is not supported as an evidence-to-release measure because evidence_available_ts is explicitly missing. It should be labeled a non-default release-timestamp proxy, with its start-time semantics unresolved.

The claim that the extract has "no timestamp for certificate/specification/deviation evidence availability" is supported for the supplied header, but should be bounded as a limitation of this extract rather than proof that the underlying systems do not retain such timestamps.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration may reflect a QCore interface or snapshot-commit timestamp rather than a fabricated/defaulted release time. The apparent cycle time may therefore combine real workflow delay with delay between disposition and interface capture; the data cannot determine the relative contributions without event-level or audit timestamps.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Recast every duration derived from lab_complete_ts or qcore_release_ts as a proxy, not an evidence-to-release KPI, and obtain a small event-level audit sample containing evidence-availability, actual disposition, and interface-commit timestamps for the same batches. This would directly test timestamp semantics while avoiding overclaiming from the 02:10 cluster.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June while the request export is associated with the 24 July ProcureNet snapshot"; "Revision-B valve supply is two free units...against four units of revision-B demand"; "All four not-transferable requests are MTR-4401 servo-drive requests" — claims are tied to named files, fields, request IDs, quantities, revisions, and restrictions, with freshness counterevidence acknowledged.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "An exact join on manufacturer part numbers...retrieves every identified request" followed by eligibility checks for "quantity, reservation...revision, UOM, qualification and freshness" — separates candidate retrieval from transfer eligibility.

"Same part family means interchangeable": rejected using the revision-A versus revision-B example and policy approval requirement — tests a plausible alternative, though the claim that the remaining work is primarily master-data hygiene somewhat overstates the causal conclusion.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "local CMMS is live, so ‘actionable now’ still requires current confirmation"; "Defend only the eight-request actionable slice, not gross value" — confidence is claim-specific and explicitly downgraded for stale global stock.
"Needs check" and "Not transferable" classifications, plus live-query and approval conditions, operationally bound uncertainty rather than treating search hits as decisions.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not convert raw search hits into automatic transfers" and "Defend only the eight-request actionable slice, not gross value" — directly changes the decision and protects against unsafe transfers.
"test search on the 11 blank-MPN requests" and compare exact-join versus semantic-search recall/precision — proposes a focused, reversible pilot with a decision criterion.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity": rejected" using reserved critical-asset stock and zero stock.
"available_qty_global=-1 means zero stock": rejected" using on-hand quantities and the verification-sentinel explanation.
"Same part family means interchangeable": rejected" using revision controls; the submission also states what live CMMS or approval evidence could revive the candidates.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Manufacturer part number and revision from maintenance records"; "Live local CMMS reservation and availability query"; "Receiving engineer and qualification approval" — requests are prioritized, discriminating, and linked to specific classification changes.
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search" — identifies a focused next test rather than requesting indiscriminate additional data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "An exact MPN join resolves all 13 identified requests immediately" overstates what an identity join establishes: it retrieves candidates, while revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, quantity, and freshness still determine transferability.

"The other 11 requests require master-data hygiene, not an expensive semantic search engine" is too categorical because blank-MPN requests may genuinely benefit from semantic candidate generation, and several known-MPN requests require operational eligibility checks rather than master-data cleanup alone.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search may add material value for the 11 blank-MPN requests even if exact MPN matching handles the identified requests; the proper conclusion is a constrained candidate-generation pilot with engineering, revision, qualification, and live-availability confirmation, not that semantic search is categorically unnecessary.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Separate the 13 exact-MPN candidate matches from actual transfer approvals in the headline and quantify each candidate's eligibility status using a current CMMS availability/reservation check, while testing semantic-search precision and recall specifically on the 11 blank-MPN requests.
